title: Bài sưu tầm 129 - Passage 1: Coober Pedy: The Underground Opal Town of the Outback
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 1 — TEST 129

Coober Pedy: The Underground Opal Town of the Outback

Paragraph 1. Nearly 850 kilometres north of Adelaide, across the treeless plains of South Australia, sits one of the world's most unusual settlements: Coober Pedy. From a distance, the landscape appears almost uninhabited, dotted only with pale mounds of excavated earth and scattered mining rigs. Yet beneath the red soil lies a thriving community of around 2,500 residents. The town's modern story began in 1915, when fourteen-year-old Willie Hutchison stumbled upon glittering opal seams while searching for water alongside a gold-prospecting party.

Paragraph 2. Word of rich gem deposits drew hundreds of fortune-seekers into the harsh outback, where summer shade temperatures routinely exceed 45°C. Exhausted by dust storms and punishing daytime heat, early miners began carving living quarters straight into the pale sandstone hillsides. The practice was spearheaded by returning soldiers after the First World War, who drew directly on their experience digging protective trenches in Europe.

Paragraph 3. Over time, these basic hillside caves evolved into comfortable subterranean homes known locally as 'dugouts'. Narrow vertical shafts bored through the rock ceiling draw fresh air downward while allowing stale indoor air to escape, maintaining a remarkably stable temperature of roughly 23°C across all seasons without electric cooling. Locals even joke that the stone walls provide effortless soundproofing and shelter from desert flies.

Paragraph 4. While early settlers hacked away at soft sandstone using hand picks and small explosive charges, modern residents hire specialized tunnelling machinery capable of cutting a spacious three-bedroom dwelling in less than two weeks. Building upward into the rock also brings unexpected bonuses: anyone wanting an extra bedroom simply excavates further into the wall, and occasionally discovers a valuable pocket of opal while remodelling. Today, the underground town includes hotels, bookshops, an art gallery, and even a Serbian Orthodox church complete with carved stone pillars.

Paragraph 5. Securing reliable water proved far harder than carving shelter. For decades, residents relied on rainwater tanks and expensive deliveries trucked across hundreds of kilometres of desert. Today, supplies arrive via a twenty-four-kilometre buried pipeline tapping brackish groundwater from an ancient underground aquifer, which must pass through a desalination plant before becoming safe to drink.

Paragraph 6. Although opal mining still anchors local culture, tourism now serves as an equally vital economic pillar. Its stark, crater-dotted horizon has doubled as an alien planet in several science-fiction films. Yet visitors are urged to follow warning signs carefully: thousands of unmarked vertical mine holes remain scattered across the surrounding plains, making off-track wandering genuinely hazardous.

groups.title: Questions 8–13
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 8–13 on your answer sheet, write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 2: "Exhausted by dust storms and punishing daytime heat, early miners began carving living quarters..."
Từ cần điền: heat.
Đoạn 2: "The practice was spearheaded by returning soldiers after the First World War..."
Từ cần điền: soldiers.
Đoạn 3: "Narrow vertical shafts bored through the rock ceiling draw fresh air downward..."
Từ cần điền: shafts.
Đoạn 4: "...hire specialized tunnelling machinery capable of cutting a spacious three-bedroom dwelling in less than two weeks."
Paraphrase: under a fortnight = less than two weeks.
Từ cần điền: machinery.
Đoạn 4: "...and even a Serbian Orthodox church complete with carved stone pillars."
Từ cần điền: church.
Đoạn 5: "...via a twenty-four-kilometre buried pipeline tapping brackish groundwater..."
Từ cần điền: pipeline.
Đoạn 6: "...thousands of unmarked vertical mine holes remain scattered across the surrounding plains..."
Từ cần điền: holes.

q8.text: A teenage boy discovered opals at Coober Pedy while searching for gold with his father.

steps: Đoạn 1: Cậu bé 14 tuổi Willie Hutchison tình cờ thấy đá opal khi đang đi tìm nước (searching for water) cùng một đoàn tìm vàng, không phải tự cậu đi tìm vàng với bố.
Kết luận: Chọn FALSE.

q9.text: Indoor temperatures inside underground homes remain remarkably stable across all seasons without electric cooling.

steps: Đoạn 3: "maintaining a remarkably stable temperature of roughly 23°C across all seasons without electric cooling."
Kết luận: Chọn TRUE.

q10.text: Underground homes in Coober Pedy cost significantly more to construct today than standard surface houses.

steps: Đoạn 4: Có nhắc việc thuê máy đào làm nhà ngầm trong chưa đầy 2 tuần, nhưng không hề so sánh chi phí xây dựng nhà ngầm đắt hay rẻ hơn nhà trên mặt đất.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q11.text: The groundwater pumped into Coober Pedy can be drunk safely straight from the aquifer.

steps: Đoạn 5: Nước ngầm bị lợ (brackish), bắt buộc phải qua nhà máy khử muối (desalination plant) mới uống an toàn được.
Kết luận: Chọn FALSE.

q12.text: Film crews have used the town's unusual landscape to represent other planets.

steps: Đoạn 6: "Its stark, crater-dotted horizon has doubled as an alien planet in several science-fiction films."
Kết luận: Chọn TRUE.

q13.text: Mining opals now brings more annual income to Coober Pedy than tourism.

steps: Đoạn 6: Nêu cả khai thác opal và du lịch đều là trụ cột kinh tế quan trọng, nhưng không so sánh ngành nào mang lại thu nhập hàng năm cao hơn.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.
